title: What does incognito mode actually hide?
caption:
What does incognito mode actually hide? Less than the name says. Chrome's own incognito screen lists who might still see your activity.
Websites, your school or work, your internet provider. It only forgets on your device.
Did you think incognito hid you? Yes or no.

youtube_title_alternatives: Who Can Still See Your Incognito Tabs 😱
youtube_description:
Incognito doesn't make you invisible. So what does incognito mode actually hide?

It's printed on Chrome's own incognito screen. Under "Chrome won't save:" it lists "Your browsing history", "Cookies and site data" and "Information entered in forms". Under "Your activity might still be visible to:" it lists "Websites you visit", "Your employer or school" and "Your internet service provider".

Here's why. Incognito only forgets on your device. Google's Chrome Help page says: "While Incognito can help keep your browsing private on your device, it doesn't make you invisible." Every page you open still crosses your network to the site, and the same page says "organizations that manage your network, like your school, employer, or internet service provider, may be able to observe your activity in Incognito." It forgets for you. Not for them.

In a 2024 settlement of Brown v. Google, Google agreed to delete or remediate old private browsing data, which by "Google's current estimate" will impact "billions of event records". Google admits no wrongdoing: the agreement says "Google is not admitting any liability, fault, or violation of law."

So, did you think incognito hid you? Yes or no.

Fine print: the incognito screen, the laptop, the booths and the court folder in the video are hand-made re-creations; no real app or logo is shown. The screen text is copied from Chrome's source code (Chromium main branch, version 159.0.8135.0, a development build) on Oct 31, 2026; the Chrome on your computer may word it slightly differently, and the Help page names the same three. "Every page still crosses your network" is our plain wording for why networks may be able to observe you; this video doesn't claim what exactly each one can see. "Scrub" is our word for the settlement's deletion and remediation of data. Google agreed to the settlement, filed Apr 1, 2024, and denies all claims; this video doesn't say whether or when final approval was given. Only Chrome's wording is quoted; other browsers weren't checked.

Sources:
- Google Chrome Help, "Browse in Incognito mode" (Computer), read Oct 31, 2026: https://support.google.com/chrome/answer/95464?hl=en&co=GENIE.Platform%3DDesktop
- Chromium source, incognito new tab strings (components/new_or_sad_tab_strings.grdp), main branch, read Oct 31, 2026: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/refs/heads/main/components/new_or_sad_tab_strings.grdp
- Brown v. Google LLC, N.D. Cal. case 4:20-cv-03664-YGR, Settlement Agreement, ECF 1097-4, filed Apr 1, 2024 (copy hosted by ClassAction.org), read Oct 31, 2026: https://www.classaction.org/media/brown-et-al-v-google-llc-et-al-settlement-agreement.pdf
